reviewRequired.note: Physical in the intended nonreactive dissolution context. Source key incorrectly marks solubility chemical.

Physical sensory descriptor in the standard property classification; key marks chemical. This is classification of a stated property, never an instruction to taste laboratory substances. Acidity as reactivity is a chemical property.
Physical sensory descriptor: odour. Source incorrectly marks this chemical; observing an odour does not itself require forming a new substance. Do not deliberately smell unknown substances.
Chemical is intended if a new gaseous substance is formed. Gas release alone could also be physical, so the observation is not conclusive without context.
Chemical is intended if a reaction generates light; light emission alone is not universal proof of a new substance.
Both physical melting and chemical reaction with sodium occur; the source’s single C label records only the reaction. Accept an explanation identifying both.
Physical dispersion/mixing of syrup and milk in the intended context; the everyday word dissolved is imprecise for a complex mixture.
